title: Age-related declines in α-Klotho drive progenitor cell ... - Nature
abstract:
The document discusses the role of α-Klotho in muscle regeneration and aging. It highlights that α-Klotho expression is upregulated in young injured muscle but declines with age, leading to impaired muscle progenitor cell (MPC) mitochondrial function, increased mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) damage, and reduced cellular bioenergetics. The study suggests that α-Klotho deficiency contributes to age-related muscle regeneration deficits.

The document also touches upon the cross-talk between signaling pathways. Specifically, it mentions that Wnt/TGFβ, insulin growth factor (IGF)-1, and fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling pathways have been implicated in the anti-aging effects of α-Klotho and in age-related declines in muscle regeneration. It notes that these pathways are responsive to signals from mitochondria, particularly through reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. The user query specifically asks about the "Insulin/IGF-1 and ROS signaling pathway cross-talk in aging and longevity determination." While the document mentions IGF-1 and ROS signaling in the context of mitochondrial function and aging, it does not delve deeply into the specific cross-talk mechanisms between Insulin/IGF-1 and ROS in aging and longevity determination. It primarily focuses on the role of α-Klotho in this process.

A relevant reference found within the document's reference list is:
*   Papaconstantinou, J. Insulin/IGF-1 and ROS signaling pathway cross-talk in aging and longevity determination. *Mol. Cell. Endocrinol.* **299**, 89–100 (2009).
